linkedin.title: We need to stop treating news like a firehose.
linkedin.body:
For years, the digital news experience has been defined by volume. Platforms compete to show you the most headlines, the most alerts, and the most noise. But more information doesn't mean better understanding. In fact, it often leads to the exact opposite.

At Headlinne, our roadmap is built on a different premise. We believe personalization shouldn't just be about showing you what you already agree with. True personalization is about giving you the context you need to understand the world, without burying you in irrelevant updates.

We are moving toward a model where AI acts as a filter for substance, not just an algorithm for engagement. This means surfacing the stories that actually impact your life or your industry, and stripping away the fluff that just fills space. It is about respect for your time.

The next phase of news isn't about getting more notifications. It is about getting the right ones, at the right time, with enough clarity to actually make sense of the day.

instagram.title: SpaceX thrusters make a Tesla Roadster fly

slides.headline: SpaceX thrusters make a Tesla Roadster fly
slides.subtitle: The electric sports car uses cold gas thrusters

slides.explanation: This Roadster is not just a concept piece. It is currently traveling through the vacuum of space, far beyond the reach of any earthly road.

slides.headline: The car is still drifting in deep space
slides.explanation: While this stunt shows off new technology, the original Roadster launched in 2018 remains in solar orbit. It is still out there, continuing its silent journey.
Four independent outlets including Space.com and the BBC have verified these details. Multiple reports confirm the technology and the car's current status.

slides.subtitle: Get the full story on the Headlinne app.

instagram.caption:
Tesla just unveiled a new Roadster that uses actual SpaceX thrusters to hover and maneuver.

It is a bold mix of automotive engineering and aerospace tech.

But the real story is where the original car ended up. That first Roadster from 2018 is still drifting through space, far away from any highway.

We verified these details across four different news sources to ensure you get the facts without the hype.
